findings.description:
Heredoc stripping removes executable shell syntax as well as literal data. For example, `cat <<EOF
$(cat /root/secret)
EOF` executes an outside-path read, but the scan sees only `cat <<HEREDOC`. The regex also consumes redirections following the delimiter declaration, such as `/root/out` in `cat <<'EOF' > /root/out
text
EOF`.
findings.failure_mode: Runs accessing forbidden paths are graded without an outside_path contamination hit.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve and scan redirections on the declaration line and executable expansions in unquoted heredoc bodies; suppress only literal heredoc data.

findings.description: The unconditional `/.` exclusion skips real absolute paths, including traversal paths. `cat /../root/secret` reads `/root/secret`, but this branch discards the candidate before outside() can normalize and reject it.
findings.failure_mode: Forbidden filesystem access is accepted as uncontaminated merely by inserting `/..` before the path.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize absolute candidates before applying path exclusions. Limit the quoted relative-path-tail exception to a verified shell concatenation context.

findings.description: The new Bash hidden-token scan is case-sensitive, dropping the documented any-case check even for unambiguous path tokens. For example, `cat /workspace/Hidden/tests.py` matches neither uppercase `HIDDEN` nor lowercase `hidden`; its path is otherwise allowed.
findings.failure_mode: Access to mixed-case hidden test paths no longer marks the run contaminated.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply case-insensitive matching to the path/identifier token alternatives while retaining the intended exclusion for bare English prose.

findings.failure_mode: An agent that writes outside the sandbox with the common `cmd <<EOF > /outside/path` shape is graded contaminated: null/false, so the run is counted as a valid trial instead of excluded. Also applies to any command words after the heredoc operator on that line (`python3 - <<EOF /root/x`).
findings.suggested_fix:
Keep the opening line and strip only from its newline to the terminator, e.g. capture the opening-line remainder and re-emit it: `HEREDOC = re.compile(r"(<<-?\s*(['"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\2[^
]*)
(?:.*?
)*?\s*\3[ 	]*(?=
|$)", re.S)` with `HEREDOC.sub(r"\1", val)` (or substitute a lambda that returns m.group(1)). Add a bats/unit case `cat <<EOF > /root/x
body
EOF` expecting outside_path.

findings.description: For the Bash tool, `"hidden" in low` (case-insensitive substring) is replaced by HIDDEN_TOKEN = `HIDDEN|(?<=[/._=-])hidden\b|\bhidden(?=[/_=-]|\.[A-Za-z0-9])` (line 1329). This no longer matches the most direct probes for the hidden test set: a bare word (`grep -ri hidden .`, `ls hidden`, `cd hidden`, `find . -name hidden`), a glob (`find . -iname '*hidden*'`: preceded by `*`, followed by `*`, neither in the lookbehind/lookahead sets), or any mixed-case form (`ls Hidden`, `cat tests/Hidden_tests.py`: `HIDDEN` is uppercase-only and `hidden` is lowercase-only; nothing is case-insensitive). The pre-change check caught all of these. The file header still claims the hidden check is 'any case' except for the token shapes, which is not what the regex implements for `Hidden`.
findings.failure_mode: A transcript in which the agent searches for or enters the hidden test directory with a bare or mixed-case `hidden` word is graded as not contaminated; the run's hidden_tests score is kept and the arm's recall/pass statistics are polluted. The DEC-0551 intent (ignore 'hidden' as an English word in heredoc prose) is defeatable in the other direction by very ordinary shell usage.
findings.suggested_fix: Scan with re.IGNORECASE and only exclude the prose case explicitly: apply the token regex to `strip_heredocs(val)` with `re.I` (so command text keeps the old any-case substring semantics, including `*hidden*` and bare `hidden`), and apply the narrow HIDDEN_TOKEN shapes only to the heredoc bodies. Alternatively keep `"hidden" in strip_heredocs(val).lower()` for command text and HIDDEN_TOKEN for the heredoc remainder. Add tests for `grep -ri hidden .`, `find . -iname '*hidden*'`, `ls Hidden`.

findings.description: Two of the new quote heuristics are weaker than their comments state. (a) after_closing_quote treats any word preceded by a quote whose predecessor is not whitespace/separator as a path tail. `""/root/.ssh/id_rsa`, `''/root/x`, and `cat x>"/root/x"` (the `>` is at pos-3, `x` at pos-2) are skipped although they resolve to absolute paths. (b) in_quotes decides by parity of ALL `'` and `"` in the prefix independently, so a single apostrophe in earlier prose (`echo "don't"; ls /root`) flips every later one-component sensitive word to 'inside quotes' and it is skipped. Both only affect edge shapes (b only one-component words), so not blocking, but they are documented as rules rather than approximations.
findings.failure_mode: Occasional false negatives for /root, /home, /mnt, /media, /srv single-component accesses and for glued-empty-quote absolute paths; grade contaminated: null where a hit was expected.
findings.suggested_fix: For (a) require a non-empty token before the closing quote (scan back to the matching opening quote and reject when the quoted content is empty, or require pos-2 to be an identifier/`$`/`}`/`)` char). For (b) use a small shell-aware tokenizer (shlex.shlex with posix=True, punctuation_chars=True) to decide quoting rather than counting characters, or restrict in_quotes to quotes on the same whitespace-delimited word.
